name: Typography
summary: Typography is a set of visual classes for headings, body copy and links. Use them to set the size and weight of text without deciding what that text is. The classes carry no semantics, so a heading class on a `div` looks right and is missing from the heading list.
demoNote: No JavaScript on this page. Everything under Common mistakes is a live failure rather than a described one; example 5 needs one click of the checkbox before it fails.

contract.useWhen: Visual text classes that carry no semantics at all.
keyboard: native: reaches the links in body copy. None of the classes is a control
failureModes: a div wearing a heading class, which is styling and not a heading
opacity for muted text, which composites against whatever is behind it
sizes in px, which ignore the browser’s own default size (SC 1.4.4)
a bare vw inside clamp(), which text-only zoom does not move
letter-spacing, text-transform and text-shadow left undeclared, so the host page cascades in
a link in body copy with color alone: it owes 3:1 against the surrounding text, and an underline
a fixed height on a box of text (SC 1.4.12) — min-height is the fix
